oracleRisk.summary: On-chain enumeration on 2026-08-08 of 71 QiDao vault contracts across 12 chains found ~2,099,471 MAI of recorded vault debt in 63 debt-bearing markets. ~71.7% of that debt sits in 15 Fantom markets whose price sources all revert (Multichain-era stranded debt), and a further ~1.3% sits in other dead-oracle markets (Polygon Celsius-era cxETH/cxADA/cxDOGE/CEL/FXS/dQUICK, Polygon stMATIC, Moonbeam GLMR, BSC DODO), where liquidation, withdrawal, and borrowing are all bricked. Every live market reads exactly one Chainlink feed — or a QiDao custom composite over one Chainlink feed — and the vault contract consumes only the answer field of latestRoundData() with no staleness check, no heartbeat enforcement, and no fallback; the only remedy is an owner-gated changeEthPriceSource by QiDao Safes. No stability pool, insurance fund, or bad-debt backstop exists on any observed deployment (stabilityPool is the zero address), and deeply underwater vaults cannot be liquidated at all because the SafeMath collateral payout underflows. Direct eth_call probes on 2026-08-09 (Fantom 122814200, Polygon 91727016-91727114, Moonbeam 16786674-16786696) confirm the dead-oracle markets are uncallable rather than merely undelayed: liquidateVault reverts with empty return data inside the price read, while the identical call on a live market returns the 'Vault is not below minimum collateral percentage' require string. liquidationDelaySec is therefore recorded as 0 only on branches with at least one operable market, and is deliberately left unrecorded on the four wholly dead-oracle branches (fantom-dead-oracle-legacy, polygon-dead-oracle-legacy, polygon-stmatic, moonbeam-glmr), whose true waiting time is unbounded and cannot be expressed in a non-negative-integer field.

branches.liquidationMechanism: Designed mechanism (currently inoperative): permissionless partial liquidation via liquidateVault() — any MAI holder repays 1/debtRatio of a below-minimum vault's debt and extracts collateral worth the repayment times gainRatio/10 at the oracle price. In practice no liquidation can execute on Fantom because the oracle call itself reverts. Re-proved by direct eth_call at Fantom block 122814200 (2026-08-09) against the BTC vault 0xE5996a2c, corroborated byte-identically on a second endpoint (rpc.fantom.network): stabilityPool() is the zero address and liquidateVault(uint256) is present in the deployed bytecode, so liquidation is permissionless and dispatchable, and vault 34 is a live position (ownerOf 0xd53064c88994119c281cc9e66c01a669e4a7715d, 0.00055772 BTC collateral, 6.652475 MAI debt) — yet checkCollateralPercentage(34), checkLiquidation(34), and liquidateVault(34) all revert with empty return data, while ownerOf(999999) on the same contract still returns its ERC721 revert string, placing the failure inside the price read rather than in any require. liquidationDelaySec is deliberately left unrecorded on this branch: erc20Stablecoin.liquidateVault contains no delay, grace-period, auction, or timestamp term at all (source re-read 2026-08-09), so the branch has no positive delay to report, but liquidation here is not undelayed — it is uncallable at every block, an unbounded wait the schema's non-negative-integer field cannot express. Recording 0 would render as 'liquidation delay: none' on a branch where liquidation cannot execute.
branches.backstop: No protocol backstop: stabilityPool is the zero address on the observed deployments and there is no stability pool, insurance fund, or committed bad-debt buyer. QiDao historically settled Multichain-era bad debt ad hoc from the DAO treasury on Polygon ($668k, per DL News); the Fantom residue (~1.51M MAI) remains unsettled with the chain's tokens in dispute.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: The vault contract defines no global shutdown, settlement, or debt-socialization path. On Fantom the entire deployment is de facto frozen: dead oracles brick liquidation, withdrawal, and borrowing, and the recorded bad debt (Multichain-era, collateral devalued) remains on the books indefinitely. QiDao's site says Fantom tokens 'return to holders once its dispute is resolved' — an off-chain process, not a contract mechanism.
